The first-time CEO says her own sponsors took chances on her—and that industry leaders need to do the same to rebuild momentum for gender equity.
Jazz CEO Renee Gala has conviction in where her company is going. The cancer and neuroscience drugmaker just recorded its highest-ever total quarterly revenue, growing 16% year-over-year to $1.2 billion.
But when the conversation turns to gender equity in biopharma leadership, she knows there’s still work to be done.
“We have lost some momentum,” Gala told BioSpace earlier this month. “It’s a bit of a vicious cycle, really, because if you don’t have women on boards, then there is less momentum to pull women into C-suites. And if you don’t have women on C-suites, who are your candidates to put in the boardroom?”
Renee Gala, CEO
Jazz Pharmaceuticals
And that burden cannot just be on women to lift each other up. Gala called on men to not only support the women around them in their immediate work, but also to be curious about different leadership styles when networking.
“Women progress more slowly from the very first opportunity they’re up for promotion—and that’s a problem,” Gala said, noting that the stall isn’t because there aren’t enough ambitious or qualified women.
To help close the gender representation gap in leadership, men in biopharma must be “more willing to take chances and sponsor people that look less like them—that may have a different leadership style,” Gala continued. “It’s getting out of your comfort zone, but it’s necessary.”
“We should all be inquisitive about asking each other questions to learn,” Gala added. “It is incumbent on all of us to focus not just on ensuring that we have appropriate representation from women, but diversity in general.”
Finding your sponsors
Sponsorship is when a leader uses their position and experience to actively promote and support others’ careers, and it creates real opportunities, Gala said. A mentor, on the other hand, more simply provides advice.
“The reality is that the CEO journey starts many years before an actual search begins,” Gala added. “If you’re not receiving the opportunities to learn and the right exposure assignments and ability to have impact earlier on in your career, it makes that journey to CEO much more challenging.”
For Gala, who has 25 years of industry experience under her belt, many of her own sponsors were men who were willing to take a chance on her.
“They were men that understood what was important to me in terms of balancing my career and having a family,” she said.
But Gala also had to be willing to stand up for herself and seek the right opportunities at the right time. “I had a lot of people throughout my career that were willing to teach. I was also willing to ask, and I think that makes a big difference,” she said.
C-suite
No ‘Sunday scaries’: Claire Mazumdar on building Bicara—and knowing when to hand over the reins
Strange and bittersweet. That’s how Claire Mazumdar describes her plan to step down from the top spot at Bicara, a biotech she helped form, and head out on parental leave before transitioning into a new role.
September 30, 2026
·
5 min read
·
Gabrielle Masson
Read more
One moment in her career that stands out is when she was interviewing with Theravance Biopharma’s then-CFO Mike Aguiar. At the time, Gala had been working on M&A deals at Eli Lilly—a job she loved. But she also had one-year-old triplets at home and couldn’t fit in the travel required for due diligence.
“I told him, ‘I will work really hard for you, but at this point in my career, what I need is to have flexibility. I am not interested in traveling, but I’m really interested in having a robust, rewarding career,’” she recalled.
Gala got the job. Both Aguiar and Theravance’s then-CEO Rick Winningham not only understood what Gala had told them—they respected it.
“They gave me incredibly challenging assignments and opportunities to learn, and they knew that having the opportunity to participate in things that my kids were experiencing was very important to me,” Gala said.
Gala spent nearly 13 years at Theravance, rising in the ranks from directing financial planning and analysis to the CFO role. In 2019, Gala joined Jazz as CFO, becoming the biopharma’s president and chief operating officer at the end of 2023, and ultimately taking the reins as CEO in August 2025.
“I never saw myself necessarily as having a CEO path, but I’ve always wanted in my career to be able to have an impact,” Gala said. “Once I started working in pharma and biotech and started to feel that deep underlying purpose, I caught the bug, so to speak—I was hooked on our industry.”

ReCode CEO Suliman leaves cystic fibrosis mission in mentee’s hands
After achieving clinical validation earlier this year, ReCode Therapeutics has called up a new CEO to take on the mission of advancing programs for cystic fibrosis and primary ciliary dyskinesia through the clinic.
September 23, 2026
·
3 min read
·
Annalee Armstrong
Read more
Be curious
Under Gala’s leadership, Jazz has experienced record-setting commercial performance and recently paid out $820 million to acquire Actio Biosciences for its epilepsy programs with high unmet need—and Gala expects more activity to come. Yet despite that success, Gala said she still notices gender-based differences in how her peers interact with her.
“In my first year as CEO, I have attended some CEO retreats and conferences that have been fabulous,” she said. “But what I found really interesting is I’ve had fewer questions from my male colleagues at some of these conferences around ‘What are some of the changes that you’ve made?’ or ‘What have you done to drive strong performance at the company in your first year as CEO?’
“Whereas I would say I get that question from almost all of my female counterparts that I’ve engaged with,” she added. “If we really want more diversity, more women in leadership, we need to ensure that we’re asking the right questions and understanding what is leading to success.”
In a time when urgency for gender equity and representation seems to have waned, the Jazz CEO credits the Biotech CEO Sisterhood and its new C-Suite groups for bolstering these efforts.
“We now see a CFO sisterhood, a CMO sisterhood,” Gala said. “There’s so much momentum here and support. I’m just incredibly grateful to be a part of that community.”

Tesla says it will finally stream its next-generation Roadster event this Thursday, October 15, at 7:55 pm Central, two weeks after it was supposed to happen.
It’s the latest date in a long list of them. Tesla first showed the Roadster in November 2017 and promised production in 2020. Nearly nine years later, it hasn’t delivered a single one.
The event was originally scheduled for October 1 in Texas. On September 28, Tesla called it off, saying it had been “tracking the weather closely with local meteorologists” and that the show “can only be held outdoors.” The new date was set for October 15, and Tesla confirmed the livestream time on X last night.
An outdoor-only event tells you what kind of show this is. Tesla isn’t planning a car launch in a showroom. It’s planning a stunt.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Every Roadster delay, so far
Here’s how we got here. The production timeline first:
November 2017: Prototype revealed at the Semi event. $50,000 reservations, $250,000 Founders Series, production promised for 2020.
July 2020: Pushed to 2021.
January 2021: Pushed to 2022.
September 2021: Pushed to 2023.
May 2023: Musk said production would “hopefully” start in 2024, adding that “this is not a commitment.”
February 2024: Musk said the design goals had been “radically increased,” with a demo by the end of 2024 and production in 2025.
November 2025: Production moved to 2027 or 2028.
And then the unveil itself started slipping. A demo planned for the end of 2025 became April 1, 2026, a date Musk said gave him “deniability.” In March, it became late April. On the Q1 earnings call, it was “maybe in a month or so.” Then late May or June, then August or later as SpaceX worked on the cold gas thruster system. In mid-August, Musk teased a “flying” demo with no driver that month. That turned into October 1, which turned into October 15.
That’s at least six production slips and seven unveil dates. And this time, Tesla blamed the weather.
A thruster demo with a car attached
Everything Tesla and Musk have teased points in one direction: SpaceX cold gas thrusters. Musk has claimed 0-60 mph in under one second with them, and the demo has been scaled back from “flying” to a short hover. The demo car is reportedly remote-operated and not street-legal.
The teasers also point to a full redesign with Tesla’s angular “Cyber” styling, which we argued last month the Roadster never needed .
A recent filing for a fan-car patent to create a vacuum underneath the vehicle could also point to Tesla trying to demo the feature with some upside-down driving, which wouldn’t be the first time an automaker has attempted it.
Electrek’s Take
You would think that as someone with two referral award Roadster reservation, I would be excited about this, but I have a hard time getting excited about Thursday.
Top comment by Ethan Hawke
Liked by 6 people
Roads tend to have sand and rocks and other debris on them that would become projectiles capable of giving passersby serious injuries if anyone tried to levitate their car with a thruster outside of a press stunt. Not to mention the sound.
View all comments
What people reserved in 2017 was a car: a four-seat, 620-mile, 0-60 in 1.9 seconds electric roadster for $200,000. That was already absurd for the time, and it would still be a great car today. Nobody put down $50,000 or $250,000 for a remote-controlled prototype that hops off the ground on compressed gas for a few seconds in a field in Texas.
But that’s what this event looks like it’s built around. A cold gas thruster gets a few bursts per tank, does nothing for you on a normal drive, and adds weight and cost. It’ll make a great clip for X and do nothing for the people waiting on a car.
The thing I’d want to see Thursday is boring: a production car, a real price, a real start of production, and a straight answer on what happens to the 2017 reservations. Tesla has shown the Roadster plenty of times. It has never shipped it.

Falcora Superyacht Concept Takes Inspiration From the Falcon and Stuns With a Look That Is Unreal!
7 photos
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli
Riva Yacht has always been synonymous with some of the world’s most luxurious and high-class yachts and boats. So, for folks looking to create the superyachts of tomorrow, tossing this name onto their design is nothing new. Well, a fresh conceptual design that has hit the scene is the Falcora, bearing the Riva name even though it doesn’t exist, yet.
Folks, the first time I encountered the Falcora, I thought I was looking at some trinket that’s born through the use of some AI software. However, I was so intrigued that I chose to dive deeper, and come to find out, Falcora is actually NOT at all crafted with artificial intelligence but the hands and mind of one Tomás Vartorelli, an industrial designer from Argentina.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli Now, Riva has nothing to do with the design, but if Falcora ever makes it to the real world, I can’t see it bearing any other name. After all, Riva has been at the forefront of luxury boating and yachting for decades, and if any brand out there would be bold enough to try to build something like Falcora, it might as well be Riva.
Riva ships aren’t the largest out there either and judging by the perspective in the renderings, Falcora is clearly not the sort of ship that’s designed to keep you floating at sea for as long as possible, but rather, one that’s to be used to brandish two things: luxury and speed, even if for short bursts at a time.
I mean, every corner of this concept screams speed, with a hull that showcases shapes and cues typically spotted on supercars, maybe even F1 rides. The Falcora gets its name from the “falcon,” and everything about this species of bird is speed and precision .
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli Since all we have here is nothing but a visual exploration of design, and only the exterior, for that matter, we can start by shedding light upon the main line of the hull. When looking at the profile of the Falcora, we can see the central line flowing from the bow to the beach club, low on the ends, and rising higher in the center, giving off a shape that follows that of the beak of a falcon, maybe even its entire head.
Speaking of beaks, falcons also have those wicked nostrils, which I like to see as the turbo intakes of this magnificent natural machine of the skies, and these nostrils and their bone tubercles seem to be expressed in the shape of the individual windows integrated into the hull.
Because of this curvature to the hull, the outdoor space sitting on top may lead you to believe that it follows the same curve but doesn’t. Only the hull itself follows these lines, and this outdoor patio includes a teak flooring that does run flat. I mean, picture trying to enjoy a glass of bubbly on a curved surface as this boat rocks back and forth on the waves underneath.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli What I'm trying to figure out is how guests transition to the rear of the Falcora or the wheelhouse and main living area. But hey, as a concept, some aspects of the design are clearly not expressed or even worked out.
But, as a concept, however, designers are able to explore all sorts of ideas that we normally wouldn’t see in the real world, be it because they’re too hard to pull off, would be extremely expensive to do so, or are simply impossible to achieve. The windshield is one of those ‘impossible’ traits, with is oddly curved shape, pinched corners, and multi-axis curvature.
The superstructure that rises from the hull to above the wheelhouse is also one of those ‘impossible’ features, again, with wild lines and curves that give this ship its unique and eye-catching looks.
At the very rear of the Falcora, Vartorelli did add another outdoor space, this time, to be used for some dining, maybe even dancing under the stars , and last but not least, the presence of a beach club means that daytime fun is in the works too.
Photo: Tomás Vartorelli The rest of Falcora is, as mentioned, a mystery, with no images showcasing any exploration into lounges, staterooms, luxury bathrooms, or any other space that we find inside such vessels. This side of the story is to be explored and defined when and if this one is ever commissioned for by some billionaire.
Come to think of it, there is a clear client that I say would be interested in the Falcora and if you’re aware of the culture that revolves around the falcon in the Arab world, we could clearly see some oil sheikh showing off their wealth by cruising the coast the Palm Jumeirah or Monte Carlo aboard this yacht. I wouldn’t be surprised to see a couple of falcons circling around Falcora either.
The downside of this visually appealing design is that ship-building methods don’t seem to be able to execute something like this, because if it could, we’d be writing about it. Oh, and if the current state of the industry CAN pull something like this off, it’s bound to cost countless millions of dollars.

While industry leaders are unsure whether the U.S. or China will prevail, they are largely united in the belief that Europe is lagging behind.
European biotech executives are divided on whether the U.S. or China will be the most important source of future innovation partnerships, a BIO-Europe survey found .
The survey, published Oct. 7, attracted 81 responses, mostly from the leaders of European, privately-owned biotechs with assets in preclinical and early clinical development. After seeing a wave of deals between Chinese and Western drugmakers, some surveyed leaders believe the Asian country is on course to be the key source of partnerships in the future.
The U.S. was the most popular answer, with 29 people predicting it will be the most important source of partnerships. China followed close behind with 24. Another 12 respondents predicted that there will be no clear leader.
Europe placed a distant third, with just 11 respondents predicting the region will be the most important source of future innovation partnerships. The finding was echoed by a request to rank Europe’s competitiveness as a partnering and dealmaking hub today on a scale of one (poor) to five (excellent). Europe scored 2.8, a result that the report’s authors called “middling.”
About half of respondents believe that policy and regulatory uncertainty in the U.S. has made Europe a more attractive place to build and partner. However, Europe’s ability to seize the opportunity presented by upheaval in the U.S. is being stymied by longstanding constraints on access to capital.
Asked to name the single biggest barrier to getting deals done in Europe, 34 respondents answered the availability of capital. The next most common answers were a valuation gap between buyers and sellers and competition from Chinese assets, which were given by 13 and 12 respondents, respectively.
The perception that the availability of capital is the key barrier is reflected in answers to the question, “If you could solve one industry challenge tomorrow, which would it be?” The most common answer, given by 42 respondents, was access to capital. Clinical trial efficiency and regulatory complexity were the next two most frequent responses, given by 11 and 8 executives, respectively.
Respondents were similarly consistent in their diagnosis of why access to capital is restricted. Almost 80% said risk aversion among investors is the biggest constraint on investment in biotech today. The next most common answer—geopolitical uncertainty—was given by 7% of respondents.
This diagnosis aligns with other assessments of the barriers to biotech growth in Europe, including in the U.K. Last year, the BioIndustry Association said that “U.K. investors do not want to invest in U.K. life sciences.” The biotech trade group attributed reluctance to invest in life sciences to the “widely acknowledged” risk aversion of U.K. investors.

Firefox Launches in Android Cars as Part of Major Google Play Store Update
10 photos
Photo: Google
When it’s not breaking down Android Auto , Google is focused on several big improvements for its experiences aimed at drivers. This time, it’s Android Automotive’s turn to get the good news, as the search giant has prepared a complete Google Play Store transformation to make finding and downloading apps more convenient and straightforward.
In addition to these Google Play Store updates, Google is also announcing new major apps that are going live for cars with Google built-in, including the famous browser Firefox.
The first thing you’ll observe when launching the new Google Play Store version is that Google is now showing new categories, including featured apps, new apps, and the option to download anything with just one tap. This is a major usability improvement on Android Automotive, considering this operating system runs in cars and the interaction with the Google Play Store takes place via the infotainment screen.
Compared to Android Auto , whose brain is still an Android phone connected to the vehicle, Android Automotive runs at the car level. It doesn’t need a connected phone, and the vehicle’s hardware is responsible for handling all tasks. This is why Android Automotive can’t be retrofitted to a car and must be installed from the factory by each carmaker that partnered with Google.
Google is also advertising easier browsing thanks to improved navigation and curated collections. This means you’ll find relevant apps, including audio, video, and games, much easier, as these categories make sense for drivers.
Photo: Polestar The new Google Play Store version also comes with improvements related to the way it shows information on the screen. It’ll look at your vehicle display size, orientation, and shape, and will update the content it shows, including these categories, in a way that makes sense.
The other big news coming out today concerns the app that you can install on Android Automotive and the features they include.
Google highlighted several big names, including Ludo King and STARZ, but without a doubt, the star of the show is none other than Firefox. The Mozilla-owned browser has long been considered the top alternative to Google Chrome, and despite its market share falling below the one of Chrome and Microsoft Edge (the default Windows browser), it continues to be one of the best browsers on the market.
Android Automotive already had several browsers, including Google Chrome and Vivaldi, but the addition of Firefox is certainly good news, especially for those who were already running this browser on their computers and mobile devices.
No information was offered on the feature lineup, but I’ve reached out to the company and will update the article when and if more information is offered. Without a doubt, a must-have option is sync support, as Firefox PC and mobile users should be able to access their data effortlessly in their cars.
Photo: Polestar Google is also bringing the audio-only mode that it originally announced for Android Auto to Android Automotive.
Back in the spring, the search giant revealed that Android Auto would be getting video app support, meaning that users will soon be allowed to watch videos in their cars directly on their infotainment screens. As a safety feature, YouTube will land on Android Auto with support for playing videos only when vehicles are stationary. An audio-only mode, which developers must manually add to their apps, will allow users to continue to listen to the audio track of the video even after the vehicle starts moving.
This feature is now making its way to Android Automotive. Google says YouTube will be the first application to get it, suggesting that more video apps will receive the same capabilities shortly.
Because the audio-only feature is essentially YouTube playing in the background, you will need a YouTube Premium subscription to get this feature.
Photo: Screenshot from GMC Hummer EV channel Google says all these features will start rolling out in the coming weeks, and there’s nothing users must do on their vehicle displays to get the updates. Once the new Google Play Store experience is ready, it will be downloaded through the automatic service and installed in your car, so you’ll see the new features the next time you launch the app.
No information has been offered about the launch of the new apps, so if you’re excited about getting Firefox in your car, there’s a chance this will happen once the new Google Play Store update goes live. Considering that the term “soon” has a completely different meaning in the Google world, I wouldn’t hold my breath for the rollout, though.
As for Android Auto, Google is still working on that major update announced earlier this year. All these features are specifically aimed at Android Automotive, and this makes perfect sense, considering Android Auto doesn’t have a stand-alone Google Play Store app. To install apps on Android Auto, you must first download and install them on your smartphone. Apps with Android Auto support should then appear on your infotainment screen.

EVs are giving oil-importing countries some breathing room during the Hormuz energy crisis. Between March and August, their EV fleets displaced an estimated $20 billion worth of crude oil, according to new analysis from energy think tank Ember.
And while more countries are going electric, the US is losing ground. Fifteen countries, including India and Brazil, have overtaken it this year in the share of new vehicles sold that are fully electric.
$20 billion worth of oil avoided
Ember estimates that electric cars in oil-importing countries displaced 200 million barrels of crude oil between March and August.
That’s oil those countries didn’t need to fuel their cars while supplies were disrupted. The $20 billion figure is Ember’s estimate of the value of that displaced oil.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
China accounted for most of that, avoiding an estimated $14 billion worth of crude oil consumption. EU countries saved another $3.1 billion, with Germany and France accounting for the largest shares.
“The countries that invested in electric vehicles before this crisis are now better protected, and a growing number are following,” said Euan Graham, senior energy analyst at Ember.
“Every electric car on the road reduces exposure to volatile oil markets, and as fleets grow, so does the protection against future supply shocks. The benefits of the global shift to electric cars extend beyond cutting emissions, with implications for energy security, economic resilience and how countries position themselves in a world where dependence on imported oil carries immense risks.”
The analysis comes alongside Ember’s new EV sales tracker . It covers 56 countries that account for more than 90% of global electric car sales and more than 80% of all car sales, and estimates how much oil each country’s electric car fleet displaces.
India and Brazil pass the US
Battery electric vehicles (BEVs) made up just 6% of US light-duty vehicle sales in the first eight months of 2026, following the rollback of the federal EV tax credits in September 2025.
Of the 56 countries Ember tracks, 49 now have higher BEV sales shares than the US. Fifteen passed it for the first time this year, including India, Brazil, Italy, Malaysia, and New Zealand.
India has been ahead of the US every month since April. Brazil has also moved ahead as its EV market grows and new manufacturing capacity comes online.
To be clear, that’s the share of new vehicles sold that are fully electric. It doesn’t mean those countries are selling more electric cars overall than the US.
Japan, meanwhile, saw its BEV sales double in 2026 after introducing a policy to help buyers with upfront costs, according to Ember.
Electric car sales keep climbing
Globally, BEV sales rose 11% year over year in the first eight months of 2026. Plug-in hybrid (PHEV) sales fell 12%, and internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicle sales dropped 6%.
BEVs accounted for 18% of new car sales worldwide, up from 16% a year earlier.
But the global average only tells part of the story. Exclude China and the US, and Ember estimates that BEV sales jumped 45% across the remaining markets.
Ember says oil supply disruptions are helping accelerate EV sales in India, Chile, Australia, and New Zealand. Policies that make electric cars more affordable are also making a difference.
France’s social leasing scheme helped its BEV sales share exceed 30% for the first time. Germany saw stronger sales after introducing new consumer subsidies at the start of 2026.
Countries are also growing their domestic EV manufacturing capacity. Tata and Mahindra accounted for more than 60% of India’s EV sales in the first half of the year. Brazil is expanding as a regional manufacturing hub, and Vietnam’s VinFast is growing its overseas production footprint.

All-New 2028 Mazda BT-50 Is Less a Workhorse and More a Lifestyle Pickup Truck in Fresh Renderings
6 photos
Photo: kolesaru / Instagram
The Japanese automaker Mazda , one of the smaller ones but also one of the most beloved, is constantly looking toward the horizon – and currently they’re focused on both EVs like the Mazda 6e or CX-6e as well as lightweight sports cars like the MX-5 Miata, which is potentially going to stay light and analog plus ICE-powered.
Mazda this year focused on the introduction of the latest CX-5 compact crossover SUV to its most important regions, as well as bringing the new CX-6e alongside the Mazda 6e in places like the Old Continent. But their future plans not only include the very light Miata sports car but, as it turns out, also a heavy workhorse, the Mazda BT-50 pickup truck.
Introduced two decades ago in 2006 as a sibling of the Ford Ranger and a successor to the B-Series pickups, the Mazda BT-50 is not produced or sold in its home market because its main location is in Thailand. Currently in its third generation, the model continues to share its underpinnings with another model, this time around the Isuzu D-Max since 2020, and received a facelift in 2024.
Alas, Mazda is already contemplating the future of the BT-50, and the rumor mill firmly believes it has a future and a fourth iteration is brewing. Just like all the other generations, the new one will share its underpinnings with an existing model since Mazda can’t develop the model alone, and while we’re waiting for confirmation on the donor model, the speculation concerns either the next-gen Isuzu D-Max or a switch to a Changan model, as Mazda already collaborates with the Chinese automaker on the Mazda 6e and CX-6e.
Naturally, the rumor mill isn’t idle, either, and has asked a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators to stop dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI to envision the next generation of the Mazda BT-50. More precisely, the good folks at Kolesa , along with their resident pixel master Nikita Chuicko, aka ' kelsonik ' on social media, have imagined the next-gen truck based on the Chinese Changan Hunter pickup truck.
However, the pixel master has used Mazda’s current design language to showcase the new model, although there is no information yet about the exterior design of the upcoming truck. So, take it with a pinch of salt, but this unofficial, hypothetical design project features the signature U-shaped LED backlit grille outline, has split headlights tucked above the bumper with integrated LED fog lights, and a host of protections at the front and rear, along with side steps.
At the back, there’s an integrated bumper with a diffuser and a step, along with vertical LED taillights and a full-width LED bar plus an integrated spoiler into the tailgate. All in all, this is now akin to a lifestyle model rather than a workhorse, right? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Колёса.ру (@kolesaru)

source_document.body:
While Alnylam’s recent reduced revenue guidance spooked investors, analysts remain broadly bullish on the biotech’s commercial prospects.
Alnylam was flying high one year ago. The RNAi pioneer’s share price was rising ever closer to $500 apiece amid the rapid growth of its transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis (ATTR) franchise thanks to a March 2025 FDA nod and the progress of late-phase programs. Today, the stock has fallen to around $250.
The company’s share price collapsed when management lowered full-year guidance in July. Sales of TTR silencer Amvuttra for the second quarter fell short of analyst expectations and Alnylam reduced its full-year guidance by about $200 million. The news raised doubts about the RNAi product’s prospects in a market served by small-molecule TTR stabilizers from BridgeBio Pharma and Pfizer.
Earnings
Alnylam absorbs $10.8B blowback after cutting full-year guidance for TTR franchise
Alnylam’s revenue cut “may create a near term credibility overhang and could “raise questions on peak sales potential, even if there’s tailwinds in the competitive landscape,” according to Stifel.
July 31, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Guggenheim Securities analysts set out the concerns raised by the revised guidance in a July 31 note to investors. The cut, which happened despite Amvuttra being the “sole, differentiated modality” in ATTR cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), suggested that the commercial opportunity is smaller than expected, the drug is mispriced or TTR stabilizers are becoming the preferred modality, the analysts said.
Alnylam’s stock has yet to recover. However, while the Guggenheim team was “on the sidelines on the stock” even before the guidance cut, other analysts have retained faith in a comeback. TD Cowen assigned a $482 price target to Alnylam back in November 2025, when the stock traded above $430. The analysts reiterated the target last month, even as Alnylam traded below $250.
The debates driving Alnylam’s stock
BMO Capital Markets analysts, who began covering Alnylam in August with a $318 price target, set out three key debates about the biotech’s prospects in an Aug. 18 note to investors. Alnylam bulls and bears are split on multiple questions, the analysts said—about the size of the ATTR market, whether the company’s next-generation RNAi candidate nucresiran creates value and the likelihood of gene silencing becoming a major drug modality.
The BMO team sided with the bulls on each point, arguing that Alnylam cut its guidance because the population of patients that Amvuttra served most urgently—those for whom stabilizers hadn’t worked—"exhausted sooner than expected.” Through that perspective, the guidance cut changed the shape of the sales ramp, not the size of the opportunity.
“The path to $10 billion+ in franchise sales was never through the second-line,” the analysts wrote, “it always ran through front-line starts and expansion of the diagnosed population.”
cardiovascular disease
‘Worse than expected’ Wainua data muddies water for TTR silencers
AstraZeneca and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ data drop divulging more details from its highly watched Phase 3 transthyretin silencer trial “further confuses the picture” for Wainua when combined with the standard of care for ATTR-CM, analysts say.
August 28, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Gabrielle Masson
Read more
As the analysts acknowledge, there is another way to view the guidance cut. An Alnylam bear may argue that cutting sales guidance two quarters into the ATTR-CM launch says something about the size of the pool. Another skeptical reading is that, having burned through the second-line market, Alnylam faces the harder challenge of competing with Pfizer’s Vyndamax and BridgeBio’s Attruby for first-line patients.
Alnylam is running Phase 3 trials of nucresiran in ATTR-CM and ATTR with polyneuropathy (ATTR-PN)—the indication for which Amvuttra was first approved, back in 2022. The late-stage failure of AstraZeneca and Ionis’ Wainua in ATTR-CM in July raised questions about nucresiran, but after the dust settled, analysts became more comfortable with Alnylam’s prospects.
In a Sept. 3 note, Stifel analysts said endpoint selection and patient enrollment drove Wainua’s failure. That view, which was echoed by BMO analysts, suggests Alnylam “is positioned for success with their event-driven study that is enriched for earlier-stage patients,” the Stifel team said.
The broadening RNAi pipeline
Beyond ATTR, Alnylam is applying its technology to big markets including hypertension and Alzheimer’s disease. BMO analysts compared gene silencing today to where monoclonal antibodies were in the late 1990s. Antibody developers ignored doubters and established a new, major modality. If gene silencing biotechs do the same, “Alnylam will own the success” more than any other company, BMO analysts said.
A Phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial of blood pressure prospect zilebesiran “tests whether RNAi can be delivered to a population-scale chronic indication,” BMO analysts said. A successful readout “could unlock a significant commercial opportunity and highlight the value of Alnylam’s ex-ATTR franchise,” the analysts added in a Sept. 17 note.
Still, skepticism abounds.
Stifel analysts, also writing on Sept. 17, said they “remain cautious on the safety profile and continue to question whether the modest [blood pressure] reductions observed in [Phase 2] are sufficient to drive a clinically meaningful [cardiovascular outcomes trial] benefit.” Alnylam is betting that consistent, modest blood pressure reductions can cut the risk of cardiovascular events.
Earnings
BridgeBio continues ATTR ascent as Alnylam’s Amvuttra falls short of expectations
BridgeBio Pharma’s transthyretin amyloidosis medicine Attruby is off to a strong launch, while Alnylam lowered full-year sales guidance for competitor Amvuttra.
August 12, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
If that bet pays off, Alnylam could cement its position at the forefront of RNAi therapeutics. ADARx Pharmaceuticals’ $446.3 million IPO in September and the 2025 deal between Novartis and China’s Argo Biopharmaceutical illustrate the growing and increasingly global nature of the sector. But Alnylam was the pioneer, and its market cap is several-fold larger than its closest biotech rivals.
Having turned its first-mover advantage into a $3.3 billion cash cushion, Alnylam is considering striking deals for drug candidates and technologies for delivering therapies to new tissues, Stifel analysts said. Alnylam is looking at areas that are complementary to what it is already working on from a commercial and R&D perspective, the analysts added.
Alnylam also has opportunities to reignite enthusiasm for its internal pipeline. This year, the biotech is set to publish Phase 2 data on a bleeding disorder drug candidate, as well as Phase 1 results on Huntington’s disease and obesity programs. Alnylam is aiming to report five or more key readouts in 2027 and in 2028.

Haval H7 Goes on Sale in the Land Down Under With Two Electrified Powertrains From Less Than AU$50k
8 photos
Photo: Haval
GWM - aka Great Wall Motors - is one of the older Chinese automakers present in Australia , and the company celebrated 18 years of presence in the Land Down Under earlier this month.
The Chinese brand has decided to celebrate the milestone alongside its customers by introducing a new offer: 0.88% p.a. annual percentage rate (2.71% p.a. comparison rate) over a 36-month loan term, with no upfront deposit required and no balloon payment, for eligible models.
The latter include the Haval Jolion Hybrid, H6 gasoline, Hybrid & Hi4 PHEV, the H6GT Hybrid & Hi4 PHEV, the Tank 300 Hi4-T PHEV and 500 Hybrid and Hi4-T PHEV, plus the Cannon Alpha Hi4-T PHEV. Alternatively, customers can get limited-time driveaway savings of up to AU$4,000 ($2,800) on selected SUVs and Utes throughout October.
GWM also has a new model launch this month to complete the celebration – back in September at Australia's Everything Electric , Great Wall Motors joined other Chinese brands and introduced the Haval H7 model, promising a mid-October sales release. Well, now they intend to keep that promise and have revealed that the first batches of the all-new Haval H7 have arrived in the Land Down Under.
The company says interest is tremendous for the new H7, rising faster than for any previous GWM model, and the model has also taken center stage at GWM’s pop-up at Chadstone Shopping Center, the Southern Hemisphere’s largest shopping center. “We have high expectations for the all-new HAVAL H7, and the level of early interest shown from prospective buyers across Australia demonstrates that GWM looks to have the formula just right with this new model,” explains Steve Maciver, GWM Australia Head of Marketing & Communications.
First deliveries will start before the end of the month for the all-new Haval H7, which “offers a bolder, more confident design language, and will sit alongside the award-winning Haval H6 to further bolster GWM’s medium SUV lineup as it prepares for further growth in the country’s largest new vehicle segment.” The new SUV originally debuted in Baveno, Italy, and brings its “distinctive boxy silhouette” to Australia with four trim levels and two electrified powertrain options.
More precisely, the Lux and Vanta models are offered with both the Hybrid and Plug-in Hybrid (PHEV) configurations and GWM’s proprietary Hi4 all-wheel drive technology, which is standard throughout. The hybrid model has 182 kW or 244 hp, while the PHEV setup rocks 320 kW or 429 hp and sprints to 62 mph or 100 kph in 4.9 seconds. The plug-in hybrid model also has an electric range of 137 km (85 miles) and a kW Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) function.
Additionally, all Haval H7 models will feature a rear differential lock, the 4x4 Expert Mode, a braked towing capacity of 1,500 kg or 3,307 pounds, a full-size spare wheel, a 360-degree camera with transparent view, plus a 15.6-inch touchscreen with GWM Coffee OS featuring wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto. Pricing starts below AU$50k ($35k)!

Android Auto 18 Now Available With Hidden "Cielo" Major Update Evidence
9 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution/Google
We’ve known for a while that Google was working on a major Android Auto transformation , and it now appears that we’re getting closer to the moment it presses the go-ahead button for the production release.
Android Auto 18, which has just landed in the beta program, includes more evidence that the work is making good progress. The update isn’t ready yet, so it’s unclear if we still have any chances to get it by the end of the year.
An early 2027 release looks more likely, considering this beta build doesn’t include any features that can be enabled.
Photo: Google Cielo is coming The new interface update is codenamed Cielo and is pretty much the first major refresh since the introduction of Coolwalk.
With the debut of Coolwalk, Google divided the main UI into multiple cards, with one card assigned to every major app category. The idea was brilliant - despite looking similar to the CarPlay Dashboard - as it allowed Android Auto users to run multiple apps side by side, regardless of their screen sizes.
The navigation app takes the largest card, whereas music apps, phone calls, and calendar entries use the remaining screen estate.
With Cielo, Google is rethinking this approach. One of the biggest feature additions that will land as part of this update is support for widgets. Compared to CarPlay, where widgets are displayed on a separate screen, which you can access by swiping right, Android Auto will display widgets side-by-side with the rest of the interface.
{fulimg2}
This also happens regardless of your screen size, so the interface will be divided into multiple panels to make sure users always get access to the apps they need, such as navigation. Furthermore, the new UI will adapt to every screen, and Google specifically highlighted Android Auto’s ability to use the entire screen estate no matter the size and shape of the display.
It’s not a secret that some cars come with unusual screen shapes, and this approach has made it more challenging for Google to make Android Auto use the entire display. MINI is just one example, where the round screen displayed Android Auto only in a rectangular panel in the middle of the display. With this update, Android Auto will use the entire screen and adapt its UI to the round unit.
Android Auto 18 includes an asset called “cielo_launcher,” which is pretty much evidence that Google has started to integrate the new UI into the app. No other strings are live right now, but I expect them to debut in the coming versions, as the work on Cielo continues.
The new version includes Google Sans Flex, a font whose main attribute is that it can adjust its settings according to the display where it’s being used. This new font will be an essential part of Google’s efforts to make Android Auto easier to use on all car screens.
An APK teardown revealed that Google is also making progress on the work regarding Work Profiles. With this update, Android Auto will allow users to enable a work profile when they connect their phones to the car. This feature is specifically aimed at people who use the same device for personal and work stuff, so when you connect to Android Auto, you can enable a dedicated profile that includes only the things that you need behind the wheel.
It’s unclear how this feature is going to work, but the most convenient approach would be for Google to allow users to configure a work profile for Android Auto and then have it enabled automatically when they start the engine and fire up the application.
Photo: Google Gemini is already an essential part of Android Auto, especially after the complete retirement of Google Assistant, but Google is now ready for the next big update. Once Cielo is prepared, Gemini will get new capabilities powered mostly by access to data in other Google services, including Gmail. What this means is that Gemini will be able to provide answers and information that is located in your inbox.
For example, if someone sends you a text to ask about your next meeting, and that next meeting is already added to your calendar, Gemini can suggest a quick answer based on the information it can read from the calendar. The same for Gmail, where Gemini will be able to check your inbox for relevant data.
How to download Android Auto 18.0 beta If you want to download the new beta without being part of the testing program, you can use the APK installer on this page to do it.
You’ll need to enable permissions for the installation of apps from non-Google Play Store sources. After the download is complete, navigate to the file, tap it to initiate the update, and follow the on-screen instructions to finalize the process.
Keep in mind that this is a beta, so an increased likelihood of issues is very possible, meaning that you’re not supposed to use this build as your daily driver.

Six EVs Burn Down in Cadillac Dealership Inferno Amid GM Battery Recall
13 photos
Photo: WFAA | YouTube
Six Cadillac electric vehicles were completely destroyed, and two more were damaged after a massive fire broke out on the lot of a Cadillac dealership in Fort Worth, Texas. The blaze took the Fort Worth Fire Department exactly 17 hours and 33 minutes to completely extinguish.
Emergency crews battled the inferno caused by the fire that originated from a single SUV parked in the yard of the Cadillac dealership. The fire soon spread to the neighboring vehicles, creating a highly complex and dangerous scene.
Firefighters initially attacked the flames using standard water protocols before realizing they were battling multiple tightly parked EVs, so what would have normally been a 30-minute routine turned into a nearly 18-hour siege.
Crew members deployed specialized EV fire blankets, which helped deprive the open flames of oxygen and hold the heat at bay so other nearby vehicles could be towed to safety. However, the trapped thermal energy caused several flare-ups and reignitions throughout the night.
Photo: WFAA | YouTube Fort Worth Fire Department decided to further monitor the vehicles for several days or even weeks, because damaged lithium-ion batteries can experience delayed chemical chain reactions and spontaneously reignite even after appearing entirely extinguished.
Videos and reports from the scene indicate that most vehicles affected were Cadillac Escalade IQs. These vehicles are equipped with massive 205-kWh lithium-ion battery packs, which means that the firefighters were essentially dealing with over one megawatt-hour of concentrated energy storage.
EV battery packs are intentionally sealed and watertight so that they can be protected against various challenges that may come up during daily driving. This design prevents water from easily reaching the internal cells. However, lithium-ion battery fire s burn significantly hotter and faster than conventional internal combustion engine fires.
Six vehicles were declared total losses, and two others sustained minor exposure damage. Fortunately, no injuries were reported among dealership staff, customers, or first responders. The official cause of the initial fire remains under investigation.
Photo: WFAA | YouTube The fire occurred amid a current safety recall affecting certain 2026 model year General Motors EVs, including the Cadillac Escalade IQ , the Chevrolet Silverado EV, and the GMC Sierra EV, due to improper battery assembly components that can present fire risks.
According to GM Recall Number N262562600 with the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), a piece of equipment (a press machine) was misadjusted during scheduled maintenance. As a result, an internal high-voltage battery module component was not fully screwed down or secured in place, which can lead to puncture or damage, causing a short circuit.
While the recall sounds alarming, it only affects exactly ten vehicles in the United States. All ten rolled off the production line of GM's Factory Zero line during a very tight window between May 4 and May 15. The affected models are the Chevrolet Silverado EV , GMC Sierra EV, Cadillac Escalade IQ, and GMC Sierra EV.
